name: hcportal_generateWebAdminToken
description: Generates a short-lived one-time token (10 min) that the Flutter portal passes to the Next.js public-web admin UI via URL parameter. The browser redeems the token via publicWeb_redeemAdminToken to obtain a session cookie. Requires the caller to have AppAccessFlags bit 0 (0x00000001) set in HC.HasherKennelMap for the target kennel.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Portal device ID — passed to ValidatePortalAuth for authentication

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived device token for this SP name — passed to ValidatePortalAuth

parameters.name: kennelSlug
parameters.description: URL slug of the kennel whose website the admin wants to edit

rowsets.name: TokenResult
rowsets.description: Returned on success — one row containing the lowercase UUID token to pass in the redirect URL. On any error the SP returns the standard Success/ErrorMessage envelope instead.

columns.name: Token
columns.description: Lowercase UUID of the newly created HC.PublicWebAdminToken row — valid for 10 minutes, single use

sideEffects: Purges all expired rows from HC.PublicWebAdminToken (DELETE WHERE ExpiresAt < SYSDATETIMEOFFSET())
Inserts one row into HC.PublicWebAdminToken with a 10-minute expiry

codeSmells.detail: The purge DELETE and the INSERT into PublicWebAdminToken run outside an explicit transaction. A crash between them leaves no partial inconsistency (the purged rows were expired anyway), so the risk is negligible. Consider wrapping if atomicity ever matters.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove the Token column from the success rowset
Never change the token lifetime without updating the Next.js session cookie maxAge
Never change the auth flag from 0x00000001 without updating all callers
